nodes.label: Mountain habitat restoration

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Habitat restoration|Mountain habitat restoration_qna_000
nodes.label: Ecology
nodes.question: What broader pressures are Alpine habitats facing that affect their seasonality and habitat structure?
nodes.answer: Alpine habitats are under pressure from climate change and land-use modifications, which lead to changes in seasonality, habitat structure, and eventually to population declines.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Habitat restoration|Mountain habitat restoration_qna_001
nodes.label: Ecology
nodes.question: How do topographic characteristics affect bird breeding success?
nodes.answer: Topographic characteristics such as elevation, slope, and aspect can influence the microhabitat and microclimate of a nest, which in turn can affect incubation behavior and breeding success in high-Alpine bird species.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Habitat restoration|Mountain habitat restoration_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What drives the abundance and accessibility of food resources in Alpine environments?
nodes.answer: Vegetation development, which generally follows snowmelt, drives the abundance and accessibility of food resources in Alpine environments.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Habitat restoration|Mountain habitat restoration_qna_003
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What type of habitats were the high-altitude populations sampled from?
nodes.answer: The high-altitude populations were sampled from unfertilized alpine meadows in the central Alps.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Habitat restoration|Mountain habitat restoration_qna_004
nodes.label: Ecology and conservation
nodes.question: Between which elevational ranges were healthier M. aculeata populations found?
nodes.answer: Healthier M. aculeata populations were found in the middle elevational range of 3700 m to 4100 m.
